ownership: Canonical declaring package/app Then namespace and internal definition/scope associations. Named applications share saved CSS with independent compiler-owned root/part hook instances. Names serve semantic reuse; source associations do not force provider-job boundaries or retry targets.
output: Accepted scoped CSS + one small generated record containing canonical scope, relevant input digest, selected/effective agent identity and host-chosen artifact path; the custom MCP server validates submitted content and writes isolated candidate CSS/provenance/metadata, separate from accepted output.
generation_inputs: static component structure and style hooks for the scope
shared renderer/theme asset versions relevant to those templates
effective generator/model recipe captured for each explicit attempt, separate from ordinary-build source/target compatibility
ordinary_builds: Consume current tracked CSS without AI calls or generation credentials. Validate relevant source/template/theme/target compatibility; missing/stale source inputs diagnose. Direct CSS edits are permitted and marked modified since generation. Changing configured provider/model only affects future generation and reports recipe drift, never silently replaces or invalidates otherwise compatible current CSS.
regeneration: Explicit headless preparation launches an enforced read-only/no-write build-time generator that submits CSS/content against server-issued logical targets through the custom MCP server. The host writes candidates; the user-facing authoring agent can inspect/check and accept them through existing controls. No required human preview/approval; failure retains current output.
application_boundary: existing source owns composition, data, bindings, permissions, forms/errors/focus behavior; generation emits scoped presentation CSS for the declared subtree

agent_selection.required_outcome: Use the shared frontend coding-agent profile by default when agent is omitted. Identify the effective agent in the saved result without requiring repetitive source attributes; do not implicitly inherit the active chat agent.
agent_selection.candidate: Accepted optional owning source profile reference, resolved through can.gen.toml; provider/model settings normally live in tooling config.
agent_selection.alternative: Optional explicit generation-command profile/tool/model override, recorded for that attempt; see docs/design/proposals/build-generation/proposal.json.
agent_selection.profile_contents: Provider, requested model/version, coding-agent recipe/tool versions and effective generation settings; secrets are environment bindings, never generated source.
agent_selection.saved_identity: Record selected profile and effective recipe, requested provider/model and actual provider-reported model/version when available. Mark unavailable resolved identity rather than claiming it was pinned.
agent_selection.status: Accepted run profile > owning declaration agent > category default; frontend uses its configured complete pair or shared. No provider or coding agent invoked.
agent_selection.default: frontend; authors need no agent= attribute or --agent flag for ordinary styling generation

lifecycle.status: Inspect accepted result, current/stale/missing status, saved agent identity and any pending or failed attempt.
lifecycle.generate: Explicitly capture the current scope inputs and effective agent recipe, then create a new candidate. Use this for first output, changed prompts or a deliberate new design; it can run even when accepted output is current.
lifecycle.retry: Selected D6 v1: Given preparation precedes dependent frontend consumers; jobs group by compatible effective complete recipe and every frontend job receives whole-Then context plus all style/view intents/use contracts. All required full-retry outputs validate and accept together under one run journal. Incomplete/failed/conflicting sets preserve every current group; recovery restores the whole old set before commit or finishes the whole new set after commit. Selective refinement retains its declared scope. One CLI job may make many model/tool calls. Full retry freshly regenerates every current prompt including preferred styles, without per-prompt IDs/names.
lifecycle.reset: Fence/discard pending work at its declared scope while preserving current CSS/direct edits; no AI call. Selective reset remains available and incomplete full-retry sets never promote.
lifecycle.accept: Selected D6 v1: Given preparation precedes dependent frontend consumers; jobs group by compatible effective complete recipe and every frontend job receives whole-Then context plus all style/view intents/use contracts. All required full-retry outputs validate and accept together under one run journal. Incomplete/failed/conflicting sets preserve every current group; recovery restores the whole old set before commit or finishes the whole new set after commit. Selective refinement retains its declared scope. One CLI job may make many model/tool calls.
lifecycle.rollback: Restore an earlier accepted CSS/record pair through retained source-control history; diagnose incompatibility with current relevant inputs rather than silently using stale output.
lifecycle.shared_defaults: Removing a component inline prompt or named attachment is an explicit authoring change; deleting saved CSS alone yields missing output rather than regeneration.
lifecycle.failure: Provider failure, timeout, rejected output or cancellation retains accepted CSS. An unknown provider outcome is shown as unknown; recover by provider attempt/request identity where supported, otherwise require an explicit fresh retry with possible duplicate cost visible.
lifecycle.refine: Capture current edited CSS, owning intent/templates/theme and refinement instruction; generate an isolated candidate from that baseline.

syntax_forms.shared_behavior: Named definitions and inline attachments share saved-output lifecycle and frontend default. Named applications reuse their definition CSS without per-use AI calls. Each full manual retry regenerates all current prompts in the active app/build scope; provider-job grouping follows frozen D6.
syntax_forms.name: Reusable local definition name in owning package/app Then namespace, not a mere label. No exports, parameters or inheritance initially. Duplicate/unknown names and incompatible application contracts diagnose.
syntax_forms.application: Top-level style Name $"prompt" defines reusable CSS without a visual body. Ordinary rendered components/pages/custom instances carry one $"prompt" or $Name suffix; nonvisual declarations and top-level anonymous scopes are excluded. Ordinary wrappers are superseded. Generated view renderer prompts stay in the view header, with one optional second $"prompt" or $Name suffix on that header for renderer-root styling and canonical controls as its only children; no inline, wrapper or leaf style statement exists. Compatible named uses share CSS without AI or copied outputs, with separate checked root/part instances; caller styling respects child-host/interior ownership.
syntax_forms.agent_override: Optional owning declaration profile override follows canonical accepted precedence.

scope_identity.required_outcome: Associate named definitions and inline attachments with authoritative opaque IDs and their saved CSS/attempts. Named uses consume the definition output rather than creating units.
scope_identity.named: Resolve reusable names in the owning package/app Then namespace; duplicate/unknown definitions and incompatible application contracts diagnose.
scope_identity.inline: Tooling owns persistent internal identity exposed by structured inspect/status with owner/source mapping. Editor selection is optional, never required. Current source position alone is not a stable saved identity.
scope_identity.identity_vs_freshness: Keep block identity separate from the relevant-input digest. Editing a prompt makes the existing result stale rather than implicitly assigning another block its CSS.
scope_identity.ambiguous_edits: Do not silently attach an accepted artifact to a different block after moves, copies or ambiguous matching. Exact identity persistence and edit reconciliation remain unimplemented design work.
scope_identity.current_gap: Bounded compiler scan found source-span/process-local identities, not persisted identities stable across edits: syntax/cst.rs SyntaxNode; analysis/mod.rs NodeKey; codegen/ir.rs IrUi and view-use IDs; codegen/js.rs presentation occurrence IDs. Existing artifact source revision/maps do not bridge this gap.

custom_views: Ordinary reusable view children/instances carry $Name or $"prompt" attachments. A prompted view retains its renderer-header prompt and carries renderer-root styling as one optional second $Name or $"prompt" suffix on that header, plus checked canonical controls as its only children.
direct_refinement: Tracked editable CSS is a primary build input accessible to the .can authoring agent. Original generated identity is historical; edited bytes are not silently attributed to that generator. Full provider/config/refinement controls are in docs/design/proposals/build-generation/proposal.json.
targeting: Manual retry regenerates all current prompts in the active app/build scope, including loved styles, without per-prompt names or selection. Internal associations still support selective direct editing/refinement and affected-use reporting for reusable definitions. The frozen implementation contract selects compatible-recipe whole-Then jobs and one complete full-retry acceptance set/run journal; scoped refinement remains available. No generation per application.

generator_output_submission.status: Human-required custom MCP output-submission boundary accepted; generation engine/server/adapters unimplemented.
generator_output_submission.input: The host supplies captured generation context plus server-issued allowed logical output targets. These targets describe admitted artifacts, not filesystem paths chosen by the generator.
generator_output_submission.submission: Build-time generator agents submit structured CSS, JavaScript and other generated code/content to the custom MCP server against those allowed logical targets. They must not create their own output files or supply filesystem destinations.
generator_output_submission.host_ownership: The host validates each submission and controls correct placement, writing isolated candidate files and their provenance/required metadata. Existing validation, leases, current-input/byte/fence checks and acceptance controls govern promotion; submission alone does not accept output.
generator_output_submission.enforcement: Adapters must enforce a read-only/no-write generator environment for protected project, current-output and candidate-output files, with generic write tools and filesystem shell writes disabled for those locations. MCP alone does not isolate filesystem access, and a prompt-only promise is insufficient. Diagnose unsupported runner MCP or enforceable no-write capabilities before launching generation; do not fall back to direct generator file writes. Native CLI session/cache housekeeping may be separately isolated and is not generated application output.
generator_output_submission.lifetime: Private bounded Node tooling session; no new package or persistent daemon. Selected tools: generation_context for immutable context/handles/roles and generation_submit for batches of {target, role, content}; UTF-8 text and checked encoded assets. Transport remains adapter-specific and protected no-write enforcement gates launch.
generator_output_submission.job_grouping: Selected D6 v1: Given preparation precedes dependent frontend consumers; jobs group by compatible effective complete recipe and every frontend job receives whole-Then context plus all style/view intents/use contracts. All required full-retry outputs validate and accept together under one run journal. Incomplete/failed/conflicting sets preserve every current group; recovery restores the whole old set before commit or finishes the whole new set after commit. Selective refinement retains its declared scope. One CLI job may make many model/tool calls.
generator_output_submission.authoring_agent: The user-facing coding agent authoring .can remains permitted to inspect and directly edit primary generated files with existing participating edit leases. It is distinct from the launched build-time generator whose output must pass through MCP.

Rendered-component $"..." / $Name attachments are the only style carriers besides the top-level named definition; a generated view carries its root style as a second suffix on its header.
